newsitem.title: USA: Takeover speculation lifts State Street.
newsitem.headline: Takeover speculation lifts State Street.

text.p: Takeover speculation lifted the stock of State Street Corp Thursday with German banking giant Deutsche Bank AG emerging as a rumored suitor, traders and analysts said.
State Street was up 2-5/8 to 52-1/2 at the midsession. Earlier, the stock was halted for a trading imbalance before a resumption of trading at a price of $54.
A spokesman for State State Street was not immediately available for comment.

Takeover talk began to swirl around State Street Corp about six months ago when Bank of New York Co Inc said it has accumulated a 4.9 percent stake in State Street and wanted to raise it to 9.99 percent.

Subsequently, the Massachusetts Board of Bank Incorporation denied Bank of New York's application to raise its stake. Bank of New York sued in the federal court in Boston seeking to overturn the state body's ruling.
"State Street is clearly the highest probability bank takeover I know of," said George Salem, analyst at Gerard Klauer Mattison.
"It (State Street) is a very high quality, unique company that has a very aggressive suitor in the form of Bank of New York," said Salem.
State Street specializes in such areas as custodial services for assets, and it has become a dominant player with $3 trillion of assets under custody.
Salem said there have been rumors about a foreign bank "perhaps Deutsche Bank" being interested in State Street. "I wouldn't preclude Chase Manhattan Corp," he said.
A spokesman for Chase said the bank has a policy or not commenting on rumors.
